notable_absence.finding: DS_VERSION() is documented to return 'a string containing the Couchbase Server version' and its worked example returns the literal string '7.6.0-1886-enterprise' - i.e. on Capella this function's documented purpose and example output are themselves version/edition strings from the server/ model, even though Capella has no discrete version numbers or Enterprise/Community edition split of its own. This is adjacent to, but distinct from, the already-logged docs-issues/capella-pages-cite-server-versions.json (which is about the docs' prose citing a version, not a function whose entire documented behavior is to return one) - flagged here as a related but structurally different instance for reconciliation to consider.

cross_product_finding: Recurrence of docs-issues/capella-pages-cite-server-versions.json in multiple places on this page: EVALUATE() and EXTRACTDDL() and HASHBYTES() are each headed 'Couchbase Server 8.0'; FINDERR() is headed 'Couchbase Server 7.6.5'; the META() function description says 'If your cluster is running Couchbase Server version 7.6.2 and later, use the META() function with the SEARCH() function...'; and a note says 'Starting with Couchbase Server 8.0, you can include up to 15 XATTRs per query.' All are literal server/-style version citations on a Capella reference page.
